questions.question: The Pulitzer Prize is an award for newspaper, magazine, online journalism, literature, and musical composition achievements, It was established in ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __1917.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Pulitzer Prize is an award for newspaper, magazine, online journalism, literature, and musical composition achievements. 
 
• It was established in 1917 by provisions in the will of Joseph Pulitzer.
 
• Joseph Pulitzer was an American (Hungarian-born) politician and publisher of the *St. Louis Post-Dispatch* and the *New York World*.
 
• There is a total of 21 categories and in 20 of them, each winner receives a certificate and a US$15,000 cash award (raised from $10,000 in 2017).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• A member of the Ghadar Party in America, Indian-American journalist Gobind Behari Lal, was the first from India to win the Pulitzer Prize for journalism in 1937.
 
• He won the award for reporting with four others, for their coverage of science at the tercentenary of Harvard University.
 
• He also received the Padma Bhushan in 1969.

questions.question: Who among the following is the author of the book, 'Development as freedom'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Amartya Sen.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**

__
 
• **Development as Freedom is a 1999 book** about **international development by Indian economist and philosopher Amartya Sen**.
 
• **In it, he explores the relationship between freedom and development**, the ways in which f**reedom is both a basic constituent of development in itself and an enabling key to other aspects.**
 
• Amartya Sen, (**born November 3, 1933, Santiniketan, India**), is an Indian economist who was **awarded the 1998 Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences** for his **contributions to welfare economics and social choice theory **and for his interest in the problems of society's poorest members.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **He received many awards namely;**

 
 
• Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences (1998)
 
• **Bharat Ratna (1999)**20
 
• **National Humanities Medal (2012)**
 
• Johan Skytte Prize in Political Science (2017)

questions.question: Who among the following is known as the 'Missile woman' of India?

__

• She is known as the** ‘missile woman’ of India.**
 
• She is a scientist at the Defence Research and Development Organisation** (DRDO).**

questions.question: From which year will the Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE) start conducting Class-10 board exams twice a year, as per the approved draft norms?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 2026

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• **CBSE plans to conduct Class X board exams twice a year from 2026** to help students improve performance, aligning with the **National Education Policy (NEP) 2020** recommendations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

 
• The proposal was **discussed with the education ministry**, and a **draft policy has been uploaded on CBSE’s website** for stakeholder feedback.
 
• **Stakeholders must submit feedback by March 9, 2025**, after which the policy will be **finalized**.
 
• **In 2026, exams will be conducted in two phases:** February 17 – March 6 and May 5 – 20, spanning **34 days**.
 
• **Science, social science, mathematics, Hindi, and English exams will be held on fixed days**, while **regional and foreign languages will be conducted on a single day**.
 
• Practical and internal assessments will be **conducted only once**, and the **final candidate list will be locked in September 2025**.
 
• **No new candidates can register for the May 2026 exam** unless they are on the **September 2025 list**.
 
• The **final marksheet will be issued after the May exam**, featuring **both attempts and the best score for each subject**.

questions.question: Which location is hosting India’s first-ever coastline and waders census?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Marine National Park and Sanctuary, Jamnagar.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• **Gujarat is conducting India’s first coastline and waders census from January 3 to 5, 2025, at the Marine National Park and Sanctuary in Jamnagar.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Marine National Park and Sanctuary is India’s first designated marine national park, covering 170 km of coastline and 42 islands.**
 
• It hosts over 300 species of local and migratory birds, including rare wader birds like the Crab Plover and Great Knot.
 
• The census is jointly organized by the Gujarat Forest Department and the Bird Conservation Society of Gujarat.
 
• Activities include expert talks, bird counting, and knowledge-sharing sessions over the three-day event.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Marine National Park and Sanctuary:**__ Located in the Gulf of Kutch, it is a protected area established to conserve marine biodiversity and mangrove ecosystems.
 
• __**Jamnagar:**__ Known as a paradise for coastal birds, it supports numerous local and migratory bird species, including over 50 species of waders.
 
• __**Crab Plover (Shankhlo):**__ A rare wader bird species that thrives in Jamnagar but is seldom found elsewhere in India.
 
• __**Knowledge-Sharing Sessions:**__ These aim to raise awareness about conservation efforts and the importance of coastal ecosystems.

questions.question: What is the highest ODI total posted by an Indian cricket team, men’s or women’s, and which team did the Indian women's team surpass to achieve this?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**435/5 against Ireland**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• **India Women’s cricket team created history** by scoring **435/5** in the third ODI against Ireland, the **highest ODI total** by an Indian cricket team across men’s and women’s formats.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

 
• This total surpassed their previous best of **370/5**, achieved in the second ODI of the same series on January 12, 2025.
 
• It is only the **sixth instance in women’s ODIs** where a team has crossed the **400-run mark**, a feat previously accomplished by **New Zealand (4 times)** and **Australia (once)**.
 
• India’s score of **435/5** is now the **fourth-highest total in women’s ODIs**, behind New Zealand’s scores of **491**, **455**, and **440**.
 
• The highest men’s ODI total for India is **418/5**, scored against the West Indies in 2011, making the women’s team’s record even more significant.
 
• **Smriti Mandhana** played a key role in the historic innings with her **135-run knock** off 70 balls.
 
• Full list of India Women’s top ODI scores includes:
 
 
• **435/5 vs Ireland (2025, Rajkot)**
 
• **370/5 vs Ireland (2025, Rajkot)**
 
• **358/2 vs Ireland (2017, Potchefstroom)**
 
• **358/5 vs West Indies (2024, Vadodara)**
 
• **333/5 vs England (2022, Canterbury)**
 
 
 
• New Zealand holds the record for the **highest women’s ODI total** with **491/4** against Ireland in 2018.

questions.question: Where is Maharashtra’s first solar park, 'Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Saur Urja Park' (CSMSUP), being developed?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Solapur.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• **Maharashtra’s first solar park, “Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Saur Urja Park” (CSMSUP), is being developed in Solapur by Hazoor Multi Projects Ltd (HMPL).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• **CSMSUP has a 1.2 GW capacity and spans 4,200 acres in Solapur district.**
 
• Advanced technology, including tracking solar panels, is being used to enhance efficiency.
 
• The project aims to support India’s renewable energy goals, reduce the carbon footprint, and create economic growth in the Solapur region.
 
• HMPL plans to expand its renewable energy projects in other Indian states, including Maharashtra and Andhra Pradesh.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Saur Urja Park__

 __
 
• First solar park in Maharashtra, contributing to India’s renewable energy capacity.
 
• Includes both fixed and tracking solar panels, enhancing solar energy generation.
 
• Promotes economic development, job creation, and sustainability in the region.
 
 
 
• Hazoor Multi Projects Ltd (HMPL)__
 
 
• Collaborating with a UK-based multinational company to execute this project.
 
• Committed to advancing renewable energy projects across India.

questions.question: What is the name of the scheme launched by the West Bengal government to curb river erosion in its 2025-26 budget?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Nodi Bandhan**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• **West Bengal government launched the "Nodi Bandhan" scheme** to develop riverine areas and check erosion along the Ganga.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

 
• **Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee highlighted the scheme's dual benefits**: combating natural calamities and creating livelihoods in riverine areas.
 
• ₹200 crore allocated to address **Ganga-Padma erosion** in Malda and Murshidabad within two years.
 
• **Minister Chandrima Bhattacharya described the scheme** as interconnecting rivers and wetlands for livelihoods like pisciculture and irrigation.
 
• **₹1,500 crore required for the Ghatal Masterplan**, with ₹500 crore allocated for 2025-26 to prevent flooding in West Midnapore.
 
• Plan to implement **nature-based solutions using hydrological models** for long-term erosion control.
 
• **Political analysts view the move as a strategy** to retain support in Malda and Murshidabad ahead of the upcoming elections.
 
• The scheme aims to promote **small-scale industries related to agriculture and pisciculture** in these areas.

questions.question: Who has been reappointed as the MD & CEO of IDBI Bank for another three-year term starting March 19, 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rakesh Sharma.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• **Rakesh Sharma has been reappointed as MD & CEO of IDBI Bank for a three-year term starting March 19, 2025.**
 
• The decision was approved by the Board of Directors on January 23, 2025, with the Reserve Bank of India’s approval.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sharma’s career spans over four decades, starting with SBI, where he excelled in credit, HR, and international banking operations.**
 
• He served as MD & CEO of Lakshmi Vilas Bank (2014-2015) and Canara Bank (2015-2018).
 
• As MD & CEO of IDBI Bank since 2018, he has driven operational and financial transformation.
 
• He also holds leadership roles in EDII, IBA, IDBI Capital Markets, and IDBI Intech Limited.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• IDBI Bank__

 __
 
• Founded in 1964 as the Industrial Development Bank of India.
 
• Currently a subsidiary of LIC (Life Insurance Corporation of India).
 
• Headquartered in Mumbai.
 
 
 
• Rakesh Sharma’s Leadership__
 __
 
• His focus has been on sustainable growth, operational efficiency, and innovation.
 
• He has strengthened IDBI Bank's financial stability and overall performance during his tenure.
 
 
 
• Related Organizations__
 
 
• **EDII**: Entrepreneurship Development Institute of India.
 
• **IBA**: Indian Banks’ Association, which represents banking institutions in India.
 
• **IDBI Intech Limited**: A technology subsidiary of IDBI Bank.
